main_text.head: VERSVS PRIMVS capitis IIII,

p.i: Displicuit autem Iona displicentia magnaLectio 59. 7.Iunij., ma-gna, & iratus est.

main_text.p: Cum & in hoc primo uersu, & sequentibus, propositum nobis sit exemplum luti cum figulo, id est, creaturę cum Creatore suo cotendentis:operæpretium fuerit, primum ὑπόθεσιν[?] rem tractare: deinde, ean-dem ad θέσιν[?] fuam reuocare: ut discamus Dei iudicia adorare, & in eius beneplaci-to fuauiter acquiescere.

Diuus Hieronymus caussas displicen-tię Ionæ hisce uerbis exposuit: Vides sub-intrare Gentium plenitudinem, & illud impleri quod in Deut.31.dicitur: Ipsi me irritauerunt in iis qui non sunt Dij: & e-go eos irritabo super gentę quæ non est; super natione stulta eos ad iracundiam concitabo. desperat de salute Israelis: & magno dolore concutitur, qui erumpit in uocem: & caussas mœroris exponit, & quodammodo loquitur: Ego solus electus sum de tanto numero prophetarum, qui per aliorum salutem ruinam meo populo nunciarem.Non igitur contristatur, ut qui-

page.notes: The scan shows a small star mark at the lower left, outside the text block; it is not printed text and is left out. The Greek words ὑπόθεσιν and θέσιν are read from a small, faded scan and are marked [?]. "Iona" in the first line may be "Ionae"; it is read as printed. "meo po / pulo" is a word split across lines without a printed hyphen, so it is written whole as "populo". Possible printing errors left as printed: "cotendentis:operæpretium" has no space after the colon, and "nunciarem.Non" has no space after the full stop. Scan is slightly skewed at the top right; the heading is read from the top of the page.
